articles.title: Spotify is giving you the keys to its recommendation algorithm with US launch of ‘Taste Profile’
articles.description: Spotify is rolling out Taste Profile to Premium users in the U.S., letting listeners see how the streamer understands their tastes and use natural language to reshape their recommendations.
articles.summary: Spotify is introducing 'Taste Profile,' a feature for U.table Premium subscribers in the U.S. that reveals how the platform interprets their music preferences and allows them to refine their recommendations using natural language.
points: Spotify introduces 'Taste Profile' for U.S. Premium users.
The feature shows how Spotify understands user tastes.
Listeners can refine their music recommendations using natural language.
articles.insight: The launch of 'Taste Profile' by Spotify represents a move towards greater user-centricity in music streaming services, potentially influencing other companies to provide similar transparency.

articles.title: PitPro’s first tire-changing robot goes live in Canada
articles.description: The startup says its automated system can change four tires in under 15 minutes.
articles.summary: PitPro's first fully automated tire-changing robot is now operational in Canada, offering a faster alternative to traditional tire-changing services. The system can change up to four tires in under 15 minutes, significantly reducing service time.
points: PitPro'table first tire-changing robot operational in Canada.
Automated system can change four tires in under 15 minutes.
Revolutionizing traditional tire-changing services in the automotive industry.
articles.insight: PitPro's automated tire-changing robot could disrupt traditional tire-changing services, offering faster and potentially more reliable services, and has the potential to expand into the U.S. market.

articles.title: Comma’s hands-off driving tech under investigation after 2 fatal crashes
articles.description: The investigation involves at least some crashes where it appears drivers were using "forked" versions of Comma's software.
articles.summary: Forked versions of Comma'static's hands-off driving technology are under investigation following two fatal crashes. Some of these crashes involved drivers potentially misusing the software.
points: The investigation into Comma'static's hands-off driving technology was initiated after two fatal crashes.
The misuse of 'forked' versions of the software is believed to have contributed to the accidents.
The technology was designed to allow drivers to safely transfer control to an autonomous system while the vehicle is in motion.
articles.insight: The incidents involving Comma'static's technology highlight the importance of software safety and the potential risks associated with the misuse of autonomous vehicle technology in real-world scenarios.

articles.title: Ema raises $77M as AI starts eating into enterprise software and services
articles.description: Ema has raised $140 million to date and has more than 50 enterprise customers, including Google and Microsoft.
articles.summary: Ema, a Seattle-based AI company, has raised $77 million to date, attracting major enterprise customers like Google and Microsoft. The funding round marks the company's significant growth and investor confidence in its AI technology.
points: Ema has raised a total of $77 million.
More than 50 enterprise customers, including major players like Google and Microsoft, have chosen Ema' extranet.
Ema's AI technology is increasingly being adopted by enterprises, eating into traditional enterprise software and services.
articles.insight: The funding and client adoption indicate a growing trend of enterprises embracing AI solutions to improve efficiency and drive innovation in the industry. This shift could disrupt traditional enterprise software and services, pushing them to evolve and adapt.
